doc: The terms a clinician is likely to type, with the structure / group / concept each one SHOULD reach. Built from this project's own cited sources: the 99 published abbreviations of data/anatomy/abbreviations.json (Q236), the 23 multi-headed muscles and their heads from data/anatomy/muscle_heads_q293.json (Q293), names from data/{nerves,vascular,ligaments,bursae,skeleton,fascia}, the not-shipped findings of Q297 / Q302 / Q306, the textbook groups of Gray's 4th ed., clinical concepts, lay terms, eponyms and Hebrew. This file exists so a test can assert the coverage rather than a document claiming it: tests/test_q306.py drives the real matcher (viewer/q298/search.js under node) over every row against every page's own compiled table and requires each row to reach a structure, a group, a concept or an honest explanation. Measured in docs/research/Q306_search_coverage_audit.md: 115 of 342 rows reached something before Q306, 342 of 342 after.

fields.kind: abbr | abbr-part | part | group | group-missing | concept | lay | hebrew | structure | not-shipped | not-shipped-but-ships | muscle.
fields.expect: a regular expression over the page display name + Latin that the intended structure must match; or 'G:<group id>' for a group; or '' when the right answer is an EXPLANATION rather than a structure; or '?' when either a group or an explanation is acceptable.
fields.note: why it is in the list, where that is not obvious.

pass_rule: A row passes on a page when (a) its expected structure is in the top three ranked results, or (b) its expected group is returned, or (c) a concept entry is returned, or (d) a cited-but-not-shipped explanation is returned. A row must pass on at least one page; a row whose structure does not exist on a given page must get an explanation there, never silence.
